author: NorthEast News Desk
body: North Korea fired several short-range ballistic missiles toward the sea early Saturday, South Korea's military said. The launches were detected from the Wonsan area at about 5:20 a.m. local time, and the missiles traveled roughly 250 kilometers before falling into waters east of the Korean Peninsula.

South Korean and U.S. authorities were analyzing the flight details and shared information with Japan. Seoul convened an emergency security meeting following the launches. The U.S. Pacific Command said its initial assessment found no immediate threat to American personnel or territory, or to U.S. allies, while emphasizing continued monitoring and coordination.

The launches add a new military development to an already tense regional environment. The reported range places the weapons in the short-range category, but officials had not yet released information about missile type, altitude or launch purpose. Those technical findings, along with any statement from Pyongyang, will help determine whether the firing was a test, exercise or political signal. The episode remains developing as governments compare tracking data.
dek: South Korea said several missiles launched from the Wonsan area flew about 250 kilometers early Saturday.
headline: North Korea fires short-range ballistic missiles toward sea
